text:
alex_k: quick question — we're seeing a batch of p95 latency spikes on cross-region requests. debating two ideas: aggressive prefetch of KV/prefix cache vs sticking with session-affinity (sticky session headers) to keep clients in the same zone. thoughts?
maya_sen: can you paste a sample trace or percentiles? are spikes correlated with cold KV misses?
alex_k: here's a scrape from last hour: p50 120ms, p95 540ms, p99 1.2s. most big tails line up with first request after a scale event or after a model-pool drain. looks like cache miss + routing hop.
liam_r: two knobs: prefetch on route match (warm kv/cache when route established) or session-affinity (x-session-region header) to pin user to a zone. prefetch adds extra work and memory but reduces misses; affinity can increase hot-spotting.
sasha: +1. affinity simplest to roll out via a header we already accept. but need eviction logic for long-lived sessions to avoid capacity skew.
alex_k: imaging configs: route config boolean `enable_prefetch` and enum `affinity_strategy: none|sticky:short|sticky:long`. we could default to none.
maya_sen: telemetry note: if we flip to sticky-short, we should add per-tenant heat metrics: session-length distribution, zone-load skew, and per-route p95 delta. otherwise we'll blind-roll.
liam_r: agree. and we should have a fallback: if target zone CPU>threshold or queue>threshold, honor `prefer_cost_over_latency` and send to next best zone. basically affinity but with ejection.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout plan created by liam_r. Canary group=10% traffic to enable_prefetch=true in eu-west-1 only. ETA 2025-06-14T09:00Z
alex_k: for console UX — devx-jen, can we make the prefetch toggle visible per-route with a recommended tooltip about memory/cost tradeoffs?
devx-jen: yes — propose a two-state control and an "insights" panel that warns when skew >10% or p95 improved <5%. should include suggested rollback action.
sasha: implementation caveat: sticky headers approach requires clients to respect `x-region-hint`. some mobile SDKs strip unknown headers. need guard: server must send back `Set-Region` response header on first assignment and accept either header or cookie.
liam_r: we also need API gateway matching precedence: if route has `zone_override` we must respect it even if affinity would pick another zone. consistency rule: explicit route config wins.
maya_sen: telemetry: add tags to traces: assigned_region, assignment_reason (sticky|prefetch|manual-override), then we can split SLO by reason.
alex_k: rollout proposal: 1) add telemetry & tracing tags, 2) console toggle for prefetch + UX warnings, 3) canary prefetch in one region, 4) small sticky-short experiment (10m TTL) for heavy read routes only. rollback via console single-click.
liam_r: minor note: prefetch needs backpressure — don't prefetch for sequences >8 tokens or extremely long KV keys, else cost explodes. add heuristics: `prefetch_size_limit` and `prefetch_rate_limit`.
devx-jen: UX: show estimated cost delta (approx tokens/requests) before enabling prefetch. show historical p95 improvement if already tested in canary.
alex_k: decision? sounds like we prototype prefetch with telemetry first, then run sticky-short if skew remains.
sasha: agree. I'll open infra task for header compatibility testing with mobile SDKs.
maya_sen: I'll wire the trace tags into the dashboard and add an alert: if skew >20% for 15m AND p95 increases, fire an incident channel.
infra-bot: ci-bot: PR #4281 created: add assignment_reason tag and prefetch flags. reviewer: liam_r.
liam_r: I'll review later today. thanks all. :thumbsup:
